USD.ghi: The world’s reserve currency; strengthens when markets fear risk or the Fed keeps rates high.

EUR.ghi: The second most traded currency; sensitive to the ECB–Fed rate differential.

GBP.ghi: Volatile during the London session; sensitive to inflation and BoE interest rates.

JPY.ghi: Safe haven and carry-trade funding currency due to low interest rates; strengthens when markets panic.

CHF.ghi: Safe haven; the SNB has intervened heavily (dropped the EURCHF floor in 1/2015).

CAD.ghi: Commodity currency: usually moves with oil prices.

AUD.ghi: Commodity and risk-appetite currency; sensitive to China’s economy, iron ore and gold.

NZD.ghi: Commodity currency (dairy, agriculture); usually moves with AUD.

CNH.ghi: Traded outside mainland China; range guided by the PBoC.

HKD.ghi: Pegged to USD within a 7,75–7,85 band.

SGD.ghi: The MAS manages it via a currency basket instead of interest rates.

ZAR.ghi: Emerging-market currency: high interest rates, high volatility, wide spreads.
